title: Parameters of the reference model (snow, about 1710)

coordinate_system.axes: [x, s, z] in metres. x: athwartships, positive to port (larboard), 0 on the centreline. s: fore and aft, positive forward, s = 0 at the middle of the 28.0 m deck length between rabbets (stem rabbet at the deck s = +14.0, sternpost s = -14.0). z: up, z = 0 on the design waterline.
coordinate_system.handedness: the triple (s, x, z) is right-handed; written as [x, s, z] in all files
coordinate_system.to_gltf: glTF / game file (+Y up, metres): (X, Y, Z) = (x, z, s), bow towards +Z
coordinate_system.to_blender: Blender (Z up): (X, Y, Z) = (x, -s, z), bow towards -Y
coordinate_system.research_stations: research notes measure stations from the dead flat: s = z_df + 1.96

confidence_levels.our inference: reasoned value, not read from a source
confidence_levels.reference model: a choice of the reference model

hull.description: Profile, keel, stem, sternpost and planking of the hull. Hull surface: offsets.json.

keel_rabbet_z_at_s0_m.note: keel rabbet height at s = 0; rabbet line z = keel_rabbet_z_at_s0_m + keel_drag_per_m · s

keel_drag_per_m.note: drag 0.40 m over the 22.4 m keel

keel_depth_below_rabbet_m.note: keel 0.25 below the rabbet + false keel 0.06

stem_sided_bottom_top_m.note: stem siding at the foot / at the head

stem_moulded_m.note: stem thickness forward of the rabbet

sternpost_moulded_heel_head_m.note: sternpost aft of the rabbet, at heel / head

planking_thickness_m.note: bottom planking; added to the moulded offsets

stem_rabbet_curve_s_z_m.note: stem rabbet (s, z): quarter ellipse to the deck, then nearly upright

sternpost_rake_deg.note: from vertical, about 12° in the research notes

transom_half_breadth_z_y_m.note: half-breadth of the after end (z, y); below the first point only the deadwood

wales_from_to_projection_m.note: wale strakes: (from, to) below the deck line, projection

offsets_file.note: research table (moulded) and generator table (outside planking)

decks.description: Deck lines, camber, bulwarks, rail, ports, hatches, companion; walking test figure.

deck_at_side_s_z_m.note: main deck at side: 0.90 + 0.95 u² forward, 0.90 + 0.45 u² aft

deck_camber_m.note: camber of the beams at the reference half-breadth

camber_reference_half_breadth_m.note: half-breadth at which the camber is measured

rail_height_above_deck_s_m.note: rail above the deck at side: quarterdeck 1.7 + 0.9, waist 1.05

bulwark_thickness_m.note: planking 0.05 + top timbers 0.12, the part standing proud

rail_cap_width_m.note: bulwark 0.14 + about 8 cm overhang each side

timberhead_width_projection_m.note: top timbers seen inboard: width × projection

port_band_from_to_above_deck_m.note: painted band of the ports, scheme b

gunport_centres_s_m.note: open gunports, each side: 7 pairs at 2.45 m in the research notes

closed_gunport_centres_s_m.note: aftmost port under the quarterdeck: closed lid only

gunport_width_m.note: ports for 4-pounders 0.60 × 0.50; the model carries 6-pounder barrels of 2.0 m (deliberate)

port_lid_open_angle_deg.note: lids open above the barrel; game range 0–100

fore_hatch.note: smaller than in the research notes (space)

stern_and_head.description: Transom, counter, rudder clearances and irons, head, catheads, hawse holes.

wing_transom_z_m.note: top of the flat lower transom (wing transom)

stern_centreline_s_z_m.note: stern centreline above the wing transom: counter, then upper transom raked 8°; counter 0.85 m instead of 0.6 m so the rudder stock clears the transom

transom_round_up_m.note: round of the transom face in plan, 0.22 m over 5.1 m

counter_top_z_m.note: top of the counter = foot of the windowed transom

rudder_clearance_sternpost_m.note: sternpost face forward of the pintle axis

rudder_clearance_counter_m.note: blade top under the counter at 35°

helm_port_clearance_m.note: radial clearance of the stock in the helm port

knee_of_head_z_offset_m.note: (z, distance forward of the stem face)

fore_mast_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

fore_topmast_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

bowsprit_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

jib_boom_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

main_yard_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

fore_yard_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

main_topsail_yard_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

fore_topsail_yard_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

main_topgallant_yard_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

fore_topgallant_yard_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

spritsail_yard_length_m.note: Steel's rules (1794) applied to the hull

main_mast_head_length_m.note: masthead: 5 in per yard (lower), 4 in per yard (topmast)

fore_mast_head_length_m.note: masthead: 5 in per yard (lower), 4 in per yard (topmast)

main_topmast_head_length_m.note: masthead: 5 in per yard (lower), 4 in per yard (topmast)

fore_topmast_head_length_m.note: masthead: 5 in per yard (lower), 4 in per yard (topmast)

main_mast_s_at_deck_m.note: 0.55 L abaft the stem head (rule 2/3 L would put it on the quarterdeck break)

mast_heel_above_rabbet_m.note: heel on the keelson: floor 0.22 + keelson 0.28

lower_mast_taper_ratios.note: diameter ratios at 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, under the head, top of head

bowsprit_above_stem_head_m.note: underside of the bowsprit over the stem head

snow_mast_abaft_main_mast_m.note: radius of main mast 0.25 + snow mast 0.09 + gaff jaws

has_boom.note: false: gaff sail without boom, brailed to the mast (1700–1720)

inch_per_yard_ratio.note: one inch of diameter per yard of length

standing_rigging.description: Numbers and diameters of the standing rigging, deadeyes, ratlines, channels.

deadeye_gap_per_diameter.note: upper to lower deadeye centres, in deadeye diameters

min_rope_diameter_in_glb_m.note: lower limit of rope thickness in the game file

running_rigging.description: Running rigging with sails furled. Diameters are set in the generator code (running rigging module), collected here per rope from rigging-lines.json; belaying points below.

pin_rails_s_ranges_m.note: pin rails along the bulwark (likely anachronism for 1710)

sails.description: Furled sails in the model (roll radii); set sails estimated from the spars for the sail plan (chapter 08, sections 'Worked example: sails of the reference model' and 'Furled sails in the reference model').

furled_sail_radii_m.note: furled roll radius at the slings / at the yardarm, by yard kind

sails_set.note: false: all sails furled, ship at anchor

set_sail_estimates.note: head 0.9 × yard, foot = head of the sail below (course 0.95 × yard), yards hoisted to the working position, courses down to the rail

fittings.description: Deck fittings and guns: positions and sizes.

capstan.note: 2.35 m forward of the main mast (bars clear the ladder route)

bell.note: at the quarterdeck break (no forecastle in the model)

swivel_guns_s_m.note: s on the rails, both sides

steering.description: Two steering variants in one model: wheel (default) and deck tiller.

steering.note: default drive: wheel (c. 1703–1710); deck tiller kept as second variant

steering_wheel.note: wheel variant: wheel Ø 1.40, drum Ø 0.30, tiller 3.0 m below deck

materials.description: Paint schemes (region → material) and material settings.

schemes.note: scheme a: period proposal; scheme b: black hull

bulwarks_red_inboard.note: variant for scheme a (red ochre inboard unconfirmed)

snow_rig.note: true: snow (trysail mast abaft the main mast)

paint_scheme.note: a: period (white stuff, oiled sides, yellow and black); b: black hull

has_boom.note: false: gaff sail without boom, brailed to the mast (1700–1720)
